scraped.scraped_description: Check out Constitute to read, search, and compare the world’s constitutions!

name: Constitute Project
tagline: A comprehensive analysis of the world's constitutions to support constitutional design and inform citizens
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
academic_citations: Constitute Project database cited in constitutional law scholarship
awards: Recognized as leading constitutional research resource

policy_outcomes.description: Used as resource by Constitutional Review Commission of The Gambia
Used by Venice Commission on Democracy through Law
Used by UN Department for Peacebuilding and Political Affairs for constitution-building work
Used by UN Women for constitution work

outcome_methodology: Documented usage by government and international organizations
published_performance_metrics: Database contains 194 constitutions with detailed comparative analysis
documented_limitations: Does not capture informal constitutional practices
curation_criteria: Comprehensive inclusion of all national constitutions and constitutional amendments with expert review
contributor_governance: Academic advisory board with constitutional law experts

government_partnerships.partner: Constitutional Review Commission of The Gambia
UN Department for Peacebuilding and Political Affairs

political_relevance_summary: Addresses barriers to meaningful citizen participation in democratic decision-making by providing tools for public engagement and deliberation.

movement_building_utility.notes: Serves as an information resource for civic actors, researchers, or the public.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (5 countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability. Methodology and approach could inform similar efforts in other jurisdictions.
primary_users_or_beneficiaries: citizens seeking to participate in local democratic processes
